advisory.finding: In the new held-out test test_completed_watchdog_result_is_not_rejected_by_aggregate_runtime, the monkeypatched clock (time.monotonic returning 100.0 then 113.0) is never consumed because the fixed _run_real_guard_with_blocking_git no longer calls time.monotonic at all. The test therefore does not actually exercise/simulate a 13s aggregate runtime against the current code; it passes trivially regardless of whether any clock is read.
merged_from: The held-out test test_completed_watchdog_result_is_not_rejected_by_aggregate_runtime monkeypatches guard_test.time.monotonic with a two-value iterator (clock = iter((100.0, 113.0))), but the fixed _run_real_guard_with_blocking_git no longer calls time.monotonic() at all (the `started`/`elapsed` lines were removed). Against the current GREEN implementation the fake clock is never consulted, so the test passes purely by returning the mocked subprocess result and does not exercise any elapsed-time logic. Its regression-detection value is entirely contingent on a reintroduced defect happening to call monotonic() exactly twice; a differently-shaped elapsed-rejection defect (or one drawing the clock a different number of times) would raise StopIteration rather than assert cleanly, and the test asserts nothing about elapsed time itself.
